findings: Published historical training seal and evaluated parent runtime freeze bind cache, schema and accepted dependencies.
Old training seeds, conservative metadata exclusions and fixed synthetic seed are disjoint; one archive snapshot and two synthetic groups are specified.
Three 4 GiB available-memory checks precede attempt; probe and worker Jobs retain 2 GiB available-memory stop floor and separate cleanup checks.
Nine stage source files and 289 runtime identities matched; ten fake tests passed and no attempt marker was present.
No fit, model read, game, or merged archive output is authorized by this stage.
limitations: This reviewer did not open the real training cache, model, trace or replay; archive identity will be checked during the one permitted worker snapshot.
Memory and Job checks are sampled rather than hard real-time limits; actual Windows execution and resources remain untested.
Seed exclusions cover recognized accessible metadata and cannot exclude private, deleted or external history.
Named Job membership prevents accidental direct worker use, not malicious same-user tampering; pre/post hashes cannot exclude transient restoration.
Synthetic compatibility does not prove GPU training or competitive improvement; post-review commit and ready checks remain required.
